messages:
eli (customer): Hey - running into an intermittent 401 from the Redwood TS SDK when requests go through our Vercel Edge function + a client service worker. Happens only when the SW is active. Looks like the OPTIONS preflight is sometimes returning 304 from the CDN and the follow-up POST loses credentials.

morgan (support): Sorry you're hitting this. Can you paste the SDK version, browser & exact repro steps? Short snippets are fine.

eli (customer): SDK @ 0.12.3, browser Safari 16.5 and Chrome latest, Vercel Edge runtime. Repro: client does fetch to our Vercel edge route which proxies to api.redwood.com via the SDK in the Edge function. When the SW is enabled we sometimes get 401 on the POST. Without SW it's stable.

eli (customer): service worker fetch handler (simplified):

```
self.addEventListener('fetch', (e) => {
  e.respondWith(
    fetch(e.request)
  )
})
```

eli (customer): curl of the preflight (OPTIONS) we observed:

```
curl -i -X OPTIONS 'https://our-site.vercel.app/.netlify/functions/api' \
  -H 'Origin: https://our-site.vercel.app' \
  -H 'Access-Control-Request-Method: POST'

HTTP/2 304
cache-control: public, max-age=0
etag: W/"abc123"
access-control-allow-origin: https://our-site.vercel.app
# NOTE: missing Access-Control-Allow-Credentials on 304
```

eli (customer): then the browser sends the POST but the cookie/authorization header isn't included and server responds 401. If I make a fresh request (no SW cache) preflight is 200 with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials:true and then POST succeeds.

juan (devex): thanks for the repro. This looks like a cached/304 preflight that lost the ACA-credentials header. Browsers require Access-Control-Allow-Credentials on the preflight/OPTIONS response if credentials will be sent. If the CDN caches a preflight that didn't include that header, subsequent 304 may not surface it. Safari has been particularly picky about this.

juan (devex): Quick workarounds to try:
- ensure OPTIONS responses include `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` and `Vary: Origin` and `Cache-Control: no-store` OR `private, max-age=0` so CDN doesn't return a stale 304.
- on client, explicitly set `fetch(url, { mode: 'cors', credentials: 'include' })` so the browser attempts credentials (but this still depends on server preflight headers)
- temporarily disable SW to confirm (you did already)

morgan (support): can you paste the Edge function proxy code? We want to confirm whether the Edge function forwards preflight or handles it.

eli (customer): Edge handler (simplified):

```
export default async function handler(req) {
  // uses redwood-ts-sdk inside edge to call our internal API
  const resp = await RedwoodClient.call(req.method, req.url, { headers: req.headers })
  return new Response(resp.body, { status: resp.status, headers: resp.headers })
}
```

eli (customer): We didn't special-case OPTIONS; it should proxy through Vercel -> CDN -> origin.

tara (platform): this is likely a Vercel CDN config issue. Vercel may cache OPTIONS if headers allow. Two actionable fixes:
1) On our origin (the Redwood endpoint) return `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` for OPTIONS responses.
2) Add `Vary: Origin` so CDN caches per-origin and doesn't serve wrong ACA headers back.

tara (platform): We can also add a small middleware to the Edge function to intercept OPTIONS and respond directly with the correct CORS set (200 + ACA credentials and cache-control no-store). That avoids CDN returning 304.

juan (devex): Example minimal middleware (Edge) to short-circuit:

```
if (req.method === 'OPTIONS') {
  return new Response(null, {
    status: 204,
    headers: {
      'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': req.headers.get('Origin') || '*',
      'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials': 'true',
      'Access-Control-Allow-Methods': 'GET,POST,OPTIONS',
      'Access-Control-Allow-Headers': 'Authorization,Content-Type',
      'Cache-Control': 'no-store',
      'Vary': 'Origin'
    }
  })
}
```

morgan (support): can you try adding the middleware or patching origin headers and let us know if it stabilizes? If yes we'll file an internal runtime/CDN configuration task to make preflight non-cacheable by default for the SDK passthrough.

eli (customer): will try now. One more data point: the failing cases correlate with `If-None-Match`/ETag presence on OPTIONS. If the CDN responds 304 the ACA header is missing. So I think the `no-store` approach will solve.

juan (devex): yup that matches. Also double-check any Service Worker caching logic — SW can intercept and re-use cached OPTIONS responses if you have a runtime cache. Your simple handler shouldn't do that but worth confirming.

eli (customer): patch applied to Edge middleware to short-circuit OPTIONS -> quick test looks good, no 401s so far. Will run traffic and report back.

morgan (support): great — thanks for validating. If you see any flakes, capture a network HAR + the raw OPTIONS/POST headers and drop them here. We'll escalate to eng-runtime if needed.

tara (platform): filing task to add guidance to our docs: "Edge + SW: ensure preflight responses are not cached; add Vary: Origin and ACA-Credentials". Assign to eng-runtime if we see more incidents.

eli (customer): thanks all :thumbsup
